newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon says Israel's housing plan wrecks peace.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon says Israel's housing plan wrecks peace.

text.p: Lebanon said on Thursday Israel's decision to build homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem dealt a severe blow to the Middle East peace process and demanded the international community to immediately stop the plan.
"This decision...will have grave effects on the peace process," Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri told reporters.
Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said Israel was wrecking anew all international efforts exerted to push forward stalled peace talks in the region.

"We demand the international community, the United States which sponsors the peace talks, and the secretary-general of the United Nations to interfere immediately to stop the Israeli plan which threatens to wreck the peace process," Bouez said.
Israel's decision has sparked criticism from its key ally the United States and Palestinian warnings that it could unleash bloodshed.
Bouez warned that the Israeli decision to build 6,500 houses for Jews in Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa would "promote extermism" and lead to "a new civil war in Palestine".
Suicide bombers from the military wing of the Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas killed scores of Israeli people in a wave of attacks a year ago.

The Arab group at the United Nations decided to request a meeting of the Security Council to force Israel to rescind its decision. The Arab League will hold an emergency meeting of its permanent representatives on Sunday.
Israel says all of Jerusalem is its capital. Palestinians consider Arab East Jerusalem, which Israel seized during the 1967 Middle East war, the capital of a future Palestinian state.

Peace talks between Lebanon and Israel have been suspended for the past three years. The talks had been stalled over an Israeli withdrawal from a 15-km (nine miles)-wide south Lebanon zone which Israel occupies to ward off guerrilla raids on its northern border.
